posts.title: LG Expands Subscriptions in Southeast Asia
posts.content:
LG Electronics Expands Appliance Subscription Business Across Southeast Asia


LG Electronics is ramping up its subscription business by expanding into Southeast Asia to sustain growth amid intensifying competition.

According to LG on the 20th, the company’s subscription sales reached ₩1.13 trillion (approx. USD 820 million) in 2023—just two years after expanding subscriptions to large home appliances. In June alone, subscriptions accounted for 36.2% of sales at LG Best Shops, excluding water purifiers, ventilation systems, and CLOi robots. With its strong first-half performance, LG expects to hit a record high in subscription revenue by year-end.

LG first entered the subscription market in 2009 with water purifier rentals and has since broadened its offering to 23 products, including refrigerators, air conditioners, stylers, dishwashers, plant appliances, and service robots. Unlike traditional one-time sales, the subscription model generates higher operating margins—reportedly above 10%, compared to the 3–5% margins typical of appliance sales—by combining product use with ongoing service fees.

The business also helps stabilize revenue flows in a seasonal market, providing steady income throughout the year.

While North America and Europe remain LG’s core appliance markets, the company is increasingly focusing on Asia for future growth. Despite slight declines last year, LG’s Asian sales have steadily expanded from ₩5.7 trillion in 2020 to ₩7.8 trillion in 2022. The decision to prioritize Southeast Asia is also shaped by slowing U.S. demand, lingering economic uncertainty in Europe, and strong local competitors in those regions.

LG began subscriptions in Malaysia in 2019, expanded to Taiwan this year, and plans to enter Thailand and India before year-end. Consumer preferences in Southeast Asia are favorable, with strong interest in Korean appliances and similar consumption trends to Korea. Thailand already shows demand for small appliances like water purifiers and air purifiers, while Taiwan has a mature market for home care services.

Lower per-capita income in Southeast Asia is another driver for subscriptions, making the model attractive to younger households who may not afford upfront purchases of premium appliances. For instance, Malaysia’s GNI per capita was USD 11,780 in 2022, compared with Korea’s USD 35,990.

Operationally, LG also benefits from its regional production hubs. Refrigerators, washing machines, and air conditioners are largely manufactured in Korea, India, and Thailand—reducing logistics costs. Logistics expenses already rose 5.8% year-over-year in Q2 2025, reaching ₩1.42 trillion.

An LG Electronics spokesperson explained, “In Southeast Asia, many areas still have underdeveloped water infrastructure. We first launched water purifier subscriptions to meet demand and are now expanding into broader appliance categories.”

Industry experts note that subscription models appeal to younger consumers, particularly in their 20s and 30s, who are looking for more affordable ways to access premium appliances. With LG’s strong brand power and the groundwork already laid by rental businesses in Malaysia, analysts believe the company is well-positioned to expand its footprint in Southeast Asia.
